created_roles.name: Census Data Researcher
created_roles.description: A demographic data specialist who knows Census Bureau products and the difference between resident population and apportionment population. Retrieves the Indiana figure straight from Census.gov pages.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior Census data researcher. Task: find Indiana's 2020 Census resident population (April 1, 2020; excludes overseas federal personnel) from an official census.gov source. Method: 0) First write one 'Lookup plan' bullet: which release you will cite (2020 Census Apportionment Results or P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data), that you want the resident population concept (not the apportionment count that includes overseas personnel), and that 'date' means the release/publication date. 1) web_search for 'Indiana 2020 Census resident population census.gov apportionment' and the P.L. 94-171 redistricting release. 2) fetch_url the best census.gov page (for example the 2020 Census Apportionment Results tables, the redistricting data release, or a state profile). 3) Quote the Indiana figure exactly as shown and say whether it is resident population or apportionment population. 4) Record the page title, full URL, and the release or publication date shown on the page, and say where on the page the date appears. 5) If a second census.gov source gives the figure, record it too. Output a bulleted list: lookup plan; figure; concept; source title; URL; date; date type (release/publication/last revised); quoted passage; corroborating source if any. If the page shows no date, say so and use the release date from a census.gov press release, naming it. Do not use non-census sites as the cited source.
created_roles.goal: Set out a short lookup plan, then find Indiana's 2020 Census resident population and the exact title, URL and release date of an official Census.gov source.
responsibilities: Write a short lookup plan: release to cite, population concept, date type
Search for and fetch Census.gov pages with the Indiana 2020 figure
Record the figure, source title, URL, and release date as stated on the page
Distinguish resident population from apportionment population
Note any second Census.gov source that corroborates the figure

outputs.format: list: lookup plan, figure, source title, URL, release date, quoted passage, which population concept it is

success_criteria: A lookup plan line comes first
The figure comes from a census.gov page and is quoted from the page
The release date is stated on or alongside the page
The population concept is labelled
constraints: Use only census.gov (or its subdomains) as the cited source
Do not infer the figure from memory; quote it from the page

created_roles.name: Data Verification Reviewer
created_roles.description: An independent reviewer who rechecks figures and dates against the primary source and tests concept confusion.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior verification reviewer. You receive an evidence note on Indiana's 2020 Census resident population. Independently fetch the cited census.gov URL (and, if possible, a different census.gov page) and check: the number matches digit for digit; it is resident population, not apportionment population including overseas personnel; the date is correctly identified and is a publication/release date. Compare with the working figure about 6,785,528 and use calc for any difference. Output a memo with headings: Verdict (confirmed or corrected), Checks performed, Final figure, Final source (title, URL), Final date, Caveats. State whether you re-fetched independently. If you cannot re-fetch, say so and mark the verdict as partial.
created_roles.goal: Confirm or correct the figure, source and date before the answer is written.
responsibilities: Independently re-fetch the cited census.gov page or a second census.gov source
Confirm the number, its concept, and the date
Check the figure against the working figure of about 6,785,528 and explain any difference
Issue a verdict

outputs.format: memo: verdict (confirmed/corrected), checks done, final figure, source, date, caveats

success_criteria: Figure matched on a page re-fetched independently
Population concept and date confirmed
Any mismatch resolved or flagged
constraints: Do not just copy the researcher's note; re-fetch

created_roles.name: Final Answer Writer
created_roles.description: Assembles the verified result into a short final answer that begins with the mandated line.
created_roles.prompt: You assemble the final answer. Use only the verification verdict (and the evidence note where consistent). The answer must open with this exact line: I read "official U.S. Census Bureau source" as Census.gov data releases such as the 2020 Census Apportionment Results or the P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data; if you meant data.census.gov tables or QuickFacts or Census Bureau publications such as the 2020 Census Demographic Data Map Viewer or state profile pages, the answer below may not apply. I read "its date" as The publication or release date of the cited source; if you meant The census reference date, April 1, 2020, the answer below may not apply. Then give: the Indiana 2020 Census resident population (the verified number, as of April 1, 2020), the source title and URL, and the source's date. Add one sentence on any caveat from the verdict. Do not add new facts.
created_roles.goal: Deliver a concise, correctly opened answer with number, source and date.
responsibilities: Open with the mandated line exactly
Give the figure, citation with URL, and date
Add a brief caveat on the resident vs apportionment distinction if relevant

outputs.format: memo: opening line, answer, source, date, short note

success_criteria: First line is exactly the mandated line
Figure, source, URL and date appear and match the verdict
No new analysis

## Requirements:
R1: Give the 2020 Census resident population of Indiana (April 1, 2020 count, excluding overseas federal personnel) as a single number, confirmed against an official Census.gov source.
R2: Cite the official Census.gov source (title and URL), such as the 2020 Census Apportionment Results or the P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data.
R3: Give the date of the cited source (its publication or release date).
R4: Open the final answer with the mandated line about the reading of "official U.S. Census Bureau source" and "its date", worded exactly as given in the task.
R5: Verify the figure, the population concept and the source date independently before the answer is finalised.
R6: Plan the lookup before searching (planning): state which release is to be cited, which population concept is wanted (resident, not apportionment) and which date counts (release date), following the working interpretation.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Working interpretation figure: about 6,785,528 resident population for Indiana, April 1, 2020, excluding overseas federal personnel (to be confirmed from the source, not assumed).
- Census reference date: April 1, 2020.
- Apportionment results were released April 26, 2021 (to be confirmed from the source).
- P.L. 94-171 redistricting data were released in legacy format August 12, 2021, and in full format September 16, 2021 (to be confirmed).
- Apportionment population includes overseas federal personnel, while the resident population does not. Indiana's apportionment count is expected to be slightly higher than 6,785,528. The right figure must be reported.
- Assumption: the source date is the release date of the Census.gov release or page cited, not the reference date.
- Assumption: if sources show different releases, the primary figure comes from the cited release and the other is noted.

## Open Questions:
- question: Which Census.gov release should be cited, and which date is its date? | assumption: Cite the Census.gov 2020 Census Apportionment Results or P.L. 94-171 release, per the working interpretation, and use that release's publication date.

plan.output: list: lookup plan, figure, concept, source title, URL, release date, quoted passage, corroborating source
plan.done_when: The list starts with a lookup plan and gives one Indiana number from a census.gov page, labelled as resident or apportionment population, with a title, URL and dated release.

plan.text: [Data Verification Reviewer]: Independently verify figure, source and date
plan.title: Independently verify figure, source and date
plan.do: 1) Re-fetch the cited census.gov page independently, and a second census.gov source if possible. 2) Check the number digit for digit, the population concept, and the date type. 3) Compare with about 6,785,528 using calc and explain any gap. 4) Write the verdict memo.
plan.output: memo: verdict, checks performed, final figure, final source, final date, caveats
plan.done_when: The memo gives a verdict of confirmed or corrected, with the final figure, source title and URL, and date, and states whether the figure was re-fetched independently.

plan.text: [Final Answer Writer]: Assemble the final answer
plan.title: Assemble the final answer
plan.do: 1) Open with the mandated line exactly. 2) State the verified number, source title and URL, and source date. 3) Add one caveat sentence if the verdict gave one.
plan.output: memo: opening line, answer, source and URL, date, short note
plan.done_when: The answer starts with the mandated line, and gives the figure, the source with URL, and its date, all matching the verification verdict.

requirements.R1: Give the 2020 Census resident population of Indiana (April 1, 2020 count, excluding overseas federal personnel) as a single number, confirmed against an official Census.gov source.
requirements.R2: Cite the official Census.gov source (title and URL), such as the 2020 Census Apportionment Results or the P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data.
requirements.R3: Give the date of the cited source (its publication or release date).
requirements.R4: Open the final answer with the mandated line about the reading of "official U.S. Census Bureau source" and "its date", worded exactly as given in the task.
requirements.R5: Verify the figure, the population concept and the source date independently before the answer is finalised.
requirements.R6: Plan the lookup before searching (planning): state which release is to be cited, which population concept is wanted (resident, not apportionment) and which date counts (release date), following the working interpretation.

givens: Working interpretation figure: about 6,785,528 resident population for Indiana, April 1, 2020, excluding overseas federal personnel (to be confirmed from the source, not assumed).
Apportionment results were released April 26, 2021 (to be confirmed from the source).
P.L. 94-171 redistricting data were released in legacy format August 12, 2021, and in full format September 16, 2021 (to be confirmed).

Apportionment population includes overseas federal personnel, while the resident population does not. Indiana's apportionment count is expected to be slightly higher than 6,785,528. The right figure must be reported.
Assumption: the source date is the release date of the Census.gov release or page cited, not the reference date.
Assumption: if sources show different releases, the primary figure comes from the cited release and the other is noted.
risks: Resident population and apportionment population (which includes overseas personnel) may be confused. The verifier checks the concept, and the figure is compared with about 6,785,528.
Pages may not show a clear publication date. The fallback is a census.gov press release date, and the date type is labelled.
Census.gov may be unreachable or blocked in the run. The verdict is then marked partial, and the answer says so rather than guessing.

Several releases (apportionment April 2021, redistricting August and September 2021) carry different dates. The answer must name the one cited release. Decision point: after step 2, confirm which release the date belongs to.
The mandated opening line is long and may be altered by the writer. Reproduce it exactly.

open_questions.question: Which Census.gov release should be cited, and which date is its date?
open_questions.assumption: settled before planning: "its date" means The publication or release date of the cited source (an assumption; the answer states it)
